newsitem.title: INDIA: India CRISIL gives "FAA" rating for Kotak-Ford FD.
newsitem.headline: India CRISIL gives "FAA" rating for Kotak-Ford FD.

text.p: India's Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL) has assigned an "FAA" (high safety) rating to the proposed fixed deposit programme of Kotak Mahindra Primus Ltd (KMP).
CRISIL said in a statement that this indicates high safety regarding the timely payment of interest and principal.
A rating of "P1+" has been assigned to the firm's commercial programme of 200 million rupees indicating that the degree of safety regarding timely payment on the instrument is strong.
CRISIL said KMP has the advantage of starting business with the strong existing infrastructure, marketing and operational set-up of KMFL's (Kotak Mahindra Finance Ltd's) car business.

KMFL's management team -- responsible for KMFL becoming one of the largest players in the car financing business -- has now moved to KMP. KMP is also expected to benefit from FCC's (Ford Credit Capital Co, U.S.) backing in terms of system support, financial control and strong asset liability management in line with FCC's practices worldwide, the statement said.

KMP is strongly placed on the resources front; the high start-up networth of 1.8 billion rupees provides the company significant competitive advantage to leverage in the future. KMP enjoys a good measure of financial flexibility on account of the strength, market position and reputation of its promoters.

CRISIL said KMP is a new joint venture company between KMFL -- rated FAAA by CRISIL -- and Ford Credit International, USA (FCI), set up to undertake, retail financing of all non-Ford passenger cars and wholesale financing of dealers in India.
FCI is a wholly owned subsidiary of FCC which is the world's largest captive automotive finance company with receivables worldwide, in excess of $120 billion.
KMP commenced operations from November 1, 1996 with the transfer of the infrastructure, marketing and operational set-up of KMFL's existing car financing business, CRISIL said.
